raw_response:
I will do this year much like I did last year, because my land is only 4.1 mu and I cannot afford to gamble. I have farmed this wheat-maize land my whole life, and I look first at what worked on my own field and what the nearby people do. If a neighbor gets a full ear or a full head, I watch that. For wheat, I will not cut fertilizer too hard, because if wheat is thin through winter and spring, I cannot make it back later. I will use improved wheat seed, put more of the fertilizer down early, water a few times since I have well water, and spray a couple of times if I see aphids or disease. For maize after wheat, I will also stay with the kind most people plant, a hybrid, because it fills better and stands better than old seed. Maize eats fertilizer too, and if I feed too little, the ears come short, so I will give a solid base amount and one topdressing. My farm is small, family labor only, so I will keep the work simple: rotary tillage, a few irrigations, and no fancy changes. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose grain. That is how I keep the harvest steady.
